topPRs.title: lagoon: specify how the post-exec transaction appears on the subblock stream
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Closes part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#334.

The subblock stream carries the post-exec (`0x7D`) transaction as `diff.post_exec_tx`. The field was added without stating where it lives, why, or what a consumer may assume about it, which left the questions raised in the thread open: should it be in `transactions`, and should `metadata.receipts` cover it?

## What this does

Adds a **Subblocks** section to `lagoon/post-exec.md` that locks the current behaviour as five normative decisions. Each is paired with a rationale (explicitly marked non-normative and subject to change) and a consumer implication, so a consumer can answer "why is this field here and what may I assume about it" without asking us.

| # | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Carried in `diff`, not `transactions` — it is recomputed as subblocks are added, so it is mutable data |
| 2 | Never appears in `transactions`, in any subblock, at any index |
| 3 | Only the last subblock's value is canonical, and the stream marks no subblock as the last |
| 4 | `transactions` may be empty |
| 5 | `metadata.receipts` carries no receipt for it |

It also closes the cross-reference loop. `subblocks.md` pointed at `lagoon/post-exec.md`, but nothing in `lagoon/` pointed back. `subblocks.md` gains a **Post-execution transactions** section summarising the rules and linking to the normative statement, and its field list and consumer guarantees now say that `transactions` excludes the post-exec transaction and that `metadata.receipts` never covers it.

## One thing the issue did not list

`sdm.md` says the sequencer appends a post-exec transaction only if the refund entry list is non-empty, so `diff.post_exec_tx` can be **absent** for a perfectly valid block, and a later subblock of the same `payload_id` may introduce it. The spec now says absence is not an error, is not "not yet computed", and is not sticky.

## Verification

- All four behaviours were confirmed against `op-rbuilder`'s `builders/flashblocks/payload.rs`, not assumed: `diff.transactions` is sliced from `info.executed_transactions`, which the post-exec transaction is never pushed onto (it goes onto a clone used only for the sealed block); `metadata.receipts` is zipped from those same transactions; subblock 0 carries the deposits; and nothing gates publication on the transaction slice being non-empty.
- The sample payload in the issue decodes as RLP `[1, 4392369, [[2,42000],[3,42000],[4,42000],[5,42000]]]` — schema version 1, `blockNumber` matching the sample's `metadata.block_number`, entries with strictly increasing indices and non-zero refunds. It satisfies the envelope and SDM validity rules exactly, so **no spec/implementation divergence surfaced** and no follow-up issue is needed on that count.
- `markdownlint`, `cspell` and `doctoc` are clean, and `doctoc` touches no file outside this diff. Every relative link and anchor in both changed files resolves.

No implementation change is expected or included.

Paired with ethereum-optimism/optimism#22978, which introduces the field in the consumer-facing docs.
